page.overview:
What is Wild Pokémon?

Wild Pokémon are Pokémon that have not yet been captured by a Pokémon Trainer and are therefore usually untamed and wary of humans. They first appeared in Generation I.

Catching the different species of wild Pokémon is one of the requirements for the player to complete the Pokédex. In most cases of the core series, with Pokémon being a franchise, they serve as the "enemy" force in gameplay, as wild Pokémon must be necessarily battled to make the player's own trained Pokémon to gain levels and potentially evolve or learn new moves in order to become stronger, and be able to face Gym Leaders and other stronger Trainers to complete the game.

Wild Pokémon most commonly appear while moving around in tall grass, which are patches typically located within routes. It is also common to encounter a wild Pokémon inside of a cave, while surfing on water, or while diving or in patches of seaweed (which is a method introduced and only found in Generation III). Wild Pokémon can be also be encountered through certain methods of interacting with the environment, such as using a fishing rod in water, or having a Pokémon use Rock Smash against a pile of rocks. In rare cases, a wild Pokémon could act as a mimic and thus be disguised as an item that resembles a Poké Ball, as is the case with Voltorb and Electrode. Certain species of Pokémon require specific methods to encounter. Overall, wild Pokémon can be found in most locations, but not in outdoor areas with no tall grass, nor within most cities and towns.

At the beginning of most games, the player cannot enter the next area from their hometown without first obtaining their first partner Pokémon, as an NPC (or Professor Oak in Generation I) prevents them from progressing and warns that they need their own Pokémon for protection when they walk into tall grass.
